title: Controv. VIII: Converting grace through the Gospel — resistible or superable, effective as man obeys or resists
pass_a_gloss: VIII. Next comes the controversy on converting grace, through the Word of the Gospel, in an operation that can be resisted or overcome, and on that grace's efficacy or inefficacy, according as a person, by the power of the Gospel, can render obedience to it or, by inborn malice, can resist grace. At first sight this seems to coincide with the Arminian Controversy, Article IV, of which more at page 254 and following.
pass_b_english: VIII. Next comes the controversy on converting grace through the Word of the Gospel: an operation that can be resisted or overcome, and whether that grace is effective or ineffective, as a person by the Gospel's power can obey it or by inborn malice can resist it.
At first glance this looks like the Arminian Controversy, Article IV — of which more at p. 254 and following.
source_text: VIII. Excipit Controversia de Gratia convertentis, per Verbum Evangelii, operatione resistibili vel superabili, deque ejus efficacia vel inefficacia, prout homo in virtute Evangelii illi obsequium praestare aut per connatam malitiam Gratiae resistere potest. Quae prima fronte videtur coincidere cum Controversia Armin. Artic. IV. de qua pluribus p. 254. &c.

lemmas.gloss: operation that can be resisted or overcome

notes: Controv. print p. 54 / PDF ~155. Margins De Gratia convertentis / efficacia. Contiguous after Controv. VII tip.

choices.why: excipit = takes up / follows as the next head in the elenchus
superabilis = that can be overcome (grace conquering resistance)
